profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting in an ML systems research lab preparing a shared benchmark package for an internal reproduction milestone and a sponsor update. One workstream owns the distributed training runs on the cluster, while the other owns the experiment tracking tables and the draft benchmarking appendix. The meeting is meant to align on interfaces and handoffs for benchmarking network fabrics for data-distributed training across Ethernet and OmniPath, including what run bundle will be handed over this week, which cluster image and communication stack those runs are assumed to use, and what artifacts will be considered ready for the appendix. The agenda is to review progress on cluster-side experiments, confirm what 'the benchmark matrix' and 'ready results' mean for the handoff, decide how the shared results folder will be populated, and confirm timing for the Friday transfer. The expected outcome is that both participants leave believing they have aligned on the experiment bundle, the output format, and ownership of the comparison tables for the sponsor-facing appendix.

members.name: Dr. Maya Chen
members.expertise: Distributed deep learning, multi-node training performance, NCCL/MPI integration, cluster experiment design
members.background: Maya leads the benchmark execution workstream in a university-affiliated HPC/ML lab and previously worked on scaling studies for GPU clusters, so she is comfortable thinking in terms of scheduler jobs, cluster images, and run reproducibility at the system configuration level.
members.private_state: She wants to hand off a clean, defensible run package without reopening infrastructure discussions, and she is concerned that the appendix team may overinterpret preliminary logs before she finishes a final verification pass.
hidden_assumptions: When people say 'the benchmark matrix,' they mean the canonical cluster-side sweep of hardware fabric x communication mode x model using the current validated image, not every presentation-oriented aggregation someone might want later.
A result is 'ready' once the run family has completed and passed her lab's quick sanity checks on loss curves and throughput consistency, even if tables and figure formatting are not yet polished.

The 'OmniPath runs' refers to the reruns done last week on the refreshed Apptainer image with the updated MPI/NCCL environment, because older OmniPath logs are superseded and not suitable for comparison.
Putting outputs in the shared results folder means dropping raw per-run logs, environment manifests, and a short README there; downstream aggregation into appendix tables is someone else's step.
If a handoff is due 'Friday,' that means before she leaves the lab in Pacific time, since the cluster reruns and sanity checks are tied to her local workday.

members.name: Leo Martinez
members.role: Research Engineer for Evaluation and Reporting
members.expertise: Experiment tracking, benchmark summarization, reproducibility packaging, technical appendix preparation
members.background: Leo supports multiple ML research projects by turning experiment outputs into comparable tables and sponsor-ready reporting artifacts; he comes from an applied ML evaluation background where consistency of summary sheets and versioned result packages matters more than low-level cluster details.
members.private_state: He wants a stable input package early enough to finish the appendix tables and avoid last-minute manual cleanup, and he is worried that cluster-side reruns may slip while he still needs something he can cite as complete for the sponsor deck.
hidden_assumptions: When people say 'the benchmark matrix,' they mean the full comparison sheet needed for reporting, including the standard breakdowns by model, node count, and communication setting that feed directly into the appendix.
A result is 'ready' only when it is in the shared reporting format with aggregated values and enough metadata to paste into the appendix without revisiting raw logs.
The 'OmniPath runs' refers to the experiment family already referenced in the standing tracker from two weeks ago, because that is the named set currently connected to the draft appendix.
If someone says they will put results in the shared folder, that includes the summary CSVs, labeled comparison tabs, and updated notes in the experiment tracker, not just raw outputs.
A Friday handoff means available by end of day Eastern so he can integrate it into the weekend sponsor update branch with the rest of the reporting materials.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the benchmark matrix
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both refer to 'the benchmark matrix' as if it were a single obvious artifact.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the executed sweep definition and corresponding run bundle across fabric, comm mode, and model under the validated cluster image.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the report-ready comparison table package with the standard breakdowns needed for the appendix and sponsor update.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In research coordination meetings, 'benchmark matrix' sounds like shared project shorthand, so both hear a familiar phrase and assume the other is naming the same artifact rather than a different representation of it.

misalignment_points.topic: Which OmniPath runs are being discussed
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both mention 'the OmniPath runs' and assume they are talking about the same run set.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is referring to the rerun set executed last week after updating the container image and communication environment.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is referring to the earlier OmniPath experiment set already linked in the tracker and draft appendix.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both run sets are plausible descendants of the same experiment family and carry similar labels, so the phrase feels sufficiently specific during a fast coordination discussion even though each person anchors it to a different concrete set.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They both agree to hand over 'ready results' this week.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes 'ready' means the runs have finished, passed sanity checks, and can be shared as validated raw outputs pending downstream summarization.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes 'ready' means the results are already aggregated into the standard summary format and require no additional interpretation before inclusion in reporting.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are competent and cooperative, and 'ready' is a common status term used in lab updates; because each person's standard is routine within their workstream, neither expects it to require explicit unpacking.

misalignment_points.topic: What goes into the shared folder by Friday
misalignment_points.surface_form: They align on 'dropping everything in the shared folder by Friday.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 plans to upload raw logs, environment files, and a brief README by Friday evening Pacific, expecting Leo to generate summary CSVs and appendix-facing tables afterward.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 expects the shared folder to contain the finished summary CSVs and updated tracker notes by Friday end of day Eastern, treating the folder as the final reporting handoff point.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Shared folders are routine coordination tools, and the action sounds operationally straightforward; each person silently imports their team's normal handoff procedure into the same phrase without seeing a need to specify file granularity or timezone.
